speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether a Government survey, including employee respondents, has been conducted on perceptions of discriminatory hiring and other HR practices, as a follow-up to past surveys focusing on employer respondents; and (b) if so, when will the findings be made public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM and the Tripartite Alliance on Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) follow up on feedback and complaints about workplace discrimination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This is complemented by TAFEP's efforts to promote and advise employers on fair employment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Rather than depend on perception surveys alone, MOM relies on other indicators, too, for evidence of workplace discrimination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Discriminatory job advertisements have become rare and employment outcomes of groups, such as women and older workers, have also improved in the past decade.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe the Minister of State mentioned that 80% of jobseekers do not perceive any kind of discrimination.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just to clarify, was this a survey of both jobseekers and those already in jobs?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Did the survey cover both jobseekers and those who are already in jobs about the perception of discriminatory human resource (HR) practices?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And if it covered both, was there any difference in the findings between those who are jobseekers and those who are already in jobs about their perception of HR practices in their company?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, what was the sample size of this survey?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Fourthly, has it already been made public and, if not, will it also be published in full?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM's survey on Fair Employment Practices is nationally representative and because they provide a credible gauge of ground sentiment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As our surveys have shown, the majority of employers adopt Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But nonetheless, we recognise, too, that there will be a minority of employers who deliberately circumvent employment principles and requirements.
